settings.eyebrow: Harvest & Flame · Annual Food Festival · Riverside Park, Sept 19–21
settings.headline:
Three days of fire,
flavor, and friends.
settings.copy: Harvest & Flame is the city's biggest open-air food festival — 60+ vendors, live-fire cooking, chef demos, and a riverfront stage that runs from noon till the last plate is cleared. Come hungry. Leave full.

trust_list.text: 60+ food vendors across 12 cuisines, all in one park
Live-fire demos from award-winning local chefs
Family-friendly all weekend — kids under 12 get in free
Rain or shine: covered stages and heated tents

settings.title: A festival built
settings.intro: We measure success the way any good cook does — by how many people leave happy, full, and already planning next year.

stats.label: Plates served over the three days

settings.title: What's on
settings.intro: From wood-fired pizza to hand-pulled noodles, here's a taste of the vendors and stages you'll find across the park this September.

items.name: Ember & Oak Wood-Fired Pizza
items.description: Blistered Neapolitan pies from a 900° wood oven, topped with seasonal produce.

items.name: Noodle & Knife
items.description: Hand-pulled noodles, slow-braised broths, and chili oil made in-house.

items.name: The Smokehouse
items.description: Twelve-hour brisket, burnt ends, and house pickles. Worth the line.

items.name: Coastal Catch
items.description: Fresh oysters, ceviche, and grilled whole fish from the day's catch.

items.name: Sweet Meadow
items.description: Hand-churned ice cream, honeycomb, and warm cobblers from local farms.

items.name: The Green Table
items.description: Plant-forward plates and seasonal salads from a farm-to-fork kitchen.

settings.title: Gates open
settings.expired_text: The festival is on! Head to Riverside Park — gates are open and the fires are lit.

settings.title: More than
settings.intro: Anyone can line up food trucks. We build a weekend — with stages, demos, and a community that shows up for all of it.

features.title: Live-fire cooking
features.text: Watch chefs work over open flames — whole-animal roasts, wood-fired ovens, and grills that never go cold all weekend.

features.title: Chef demos & workshops
features.text: Eighteen hands-on demos across three days, from knife skills to sourdough. Learn something, then go eat it.

features.title: A riverfront stage
features.text: Local bands and DJs play from noon till close. Good food deserves good music, and we bring both.

features.title: Family-friendly
features.text: Kids under 12 get in free, with a dedicated family zone, face painting, and plenty of lawn to run around on.

features.title: Local first
features.text: Most of our vendors and all of our produce come from within 100 miles. You're eating the region, literally.

features.title: Rain or shine
features.text: Covered stages, heated tents, and a plan for the weather. The fires don't go out for a little rain.

settings.title: Moments from
settings.intro: A look at the smoke, the crowds, and the plates that made last year's festival one for the books.

settings.title: What regulars
settings.intro: We've been doing this for nine years, and the best part is still hearing people talk about their favorite plate.

reviews.quote: We've been every year since the first one. The brisket line is worth it, the music is great, and the kids actually have stuff to do. It's our family's September tradition.
reviews.author: Marta L.

reviews.quote: As a vendor, this is the best-run festival we do all year. The crowds are huge, the organizers are on top of everything, and we sell out by Sunday afternoon.
reviews.author: D. Reyes

reviews.quote: Came for the pizza, stayed for the chef demos. Learned how to make the sourdough I now bake every weekend. Worth every penny of the ticket.
reviews.author: Priya N.

settings.title: Come hungry,
settings.intro: Questions about tickets, accessibility, or vending? Want to bring your food truck or band next year? We'd love to hear from you.
settings.location: Riverside Park, 400 Riverfront Way · Gates open 11am daily, Sept 19–21

settings.blurb: The city's biggest open-air food festival — 60+ vendors, live-fire cooking, chef demos, and a riverfront stage, every September in Riverside Park.
